questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Vedas and Vedic Roots' refers to.
questions.a: India's oldest knowledge tradition flows from the Vedas, collections of hymns preserved for millennia by memorised recitation; they praise nature's powers and teach rita, the cosmic order of right living.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Vedas and Vedic Roots'.
questions.a: The Vedas are the common trunk of Indian culture, remembered in sound long before they were written.

concepts.title: Jainism and Buddhism: New Schools of Thought

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Jainism and Buddhism: New Schools of Thought' refers to.
questions.a: In the first millennium BCE new schools of thought arose, among them Jainism taught by Mahavira and Buddhism taught by the Buddha, both questioning ritual and preaching non-violence and ethical conduct.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Jainism and Buddhism: New Schools of Thought'.
questions.a: Seekers asked fresh questions about suffering and how to live, giving India traditions of debate and renunciation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Jainism and Buddhism: New Schools of Thought' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: The Buddha and the Middle Path

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Buddha and the Middle Path' refers to.
questions.a: The Buddha taught a middle path between harsh self-denial and indulgence, with compassion for all beings; panels and images across Asia show him seated in calm, spreading the dharma he found under the Bodhi tree.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Buddha and the Middle Path'.
questions.a: The Buddha's answer to suffering is balance and compassion, a path open to anyone who walks it.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Buddha and the Middle Path' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Folk and Tribal Traditions' refers to.
questions.a: Alongside the great schools, countless folk and tribal traditions, local deities, songs, festivals and sacred groves, shaped daily life and fed the larger currents of Indian culture.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Folk and Tribal Traditions'.
questions.a: India's culture grows from many roots: village and tribal ways are branches as real as the great texts.
